    Draft a GitHub pull request in Claude Code with a /pr slash command
    If you keep pasting the branch diff and "write a PR title and body, then wait" into Claude Code, turn that prompt into a slash command. The file name becomes the command; $ARGUMENTS lets you name the base branch or add extra instructions. Save this as .claude/commands/pr.md: --- description: "Draft a GitHub pull request from the current branch" argument-hint: "[base branch | extra instructions]" --- Draft a GitHub pull request for the current branch. Do not create it until I confirm. 1. Run `git status -sb`, `git log --oneline -15`, and `git diff origin/HEAD...HEAD` (or `main...HEAD` if `origin/HEAD` is missing). If there is no unique commit versus the base, stop and say so. 2. If I passed arguments (`$ARGUMENTS`), treat the first token as a base branch when it looks like one (`main`, `master`, `develop`, or `origin/...`). Treat the rest as extra instructions. 3. Propose a PR title and a body with a short summary, a test plan, and any follow-ups. Do not add AI attribution unless I ask. 4. Show the title and body and wait for me to confirm before running `gh pr create`. Never force-push, never merge, and never add reviewers I did not name. Use it as /pr, /pr main, or /pr develop include a migration note. Slash commands are markdown files in .claude/commands. Claude Code injects the file as the prompt and replaces $ARGUMENTS with whatever you type after the command. Keeping "wait for confirm" and "never force-push or merge" in the command reduces unattended PR creation. Pair this with an "ask" permission rule for gh pr create if you also want a permissions bump. Commit the command file so every teammate gets the same workflow. Pair with a /commit command so the branch messages and the PR body stay consistent. Two tones at f₁ and f₂ passing through a nonlinearity produce products at mf₁ ± nf₂.     What Makes a Technology Project Trustworthy?

A few practical notes from dealing with this a lot: 1. Get the file out of the Voice Memos app first. Open the memo, tap the three dots, then "Save to Files". Now it's a normal .m4a file you can pick from any browser upload button. 2. Don't go above the source quality. Voice Memos records AAC at roughly 64-128 kbps depending on your "Audio Quality" setting. Exporting that as a 320 kbps MP3 only makes the file bigger. 128 kbps is plenty for speech; 96 kbps mono is fine for meeting notes. 3. For videos, you only want the audio track. Screen recordings and camera videos are MOV files. Converting them straight to MP3 drops the video and usually shrinks the file by 90% or more. 4. Trim silence before converting. Cutting the dead air at the start in the Voice Memos editor saves a second re-encode later. 5. Rename before sharing. "2026-11-14 client call.mp3" beats "New Recording 47.mp3" when it lands in someone else's inbox. For the conversion itself you don't need an app: we wrote up how to turn iPhone voice memos into MP3 straight from Safari, and the M4A to MP3 converter it uses runs in the browser with no sign-up.     Five checks for agent memory before using it in production
    This article was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed by its author. A memory feature needs an acceptance test, not just a successful retrieval demo. Start with one small task whose answer you can check. Record its inputs, expected answer and permissions before enabling memory. Then try five cases: Recall: save a useful project fact, start a new session and check whether the agent retrieves the right source. Correction: replace that fact with a newer decision. Check that the agent uses the correction and exposes the old note as superseded. Missing context: ask about an unstored detail. The agent should expose the gap instead of treating a guess as remembered evidence. Isolation: repeat the question in a separate test workspace. Check that another workspace's private notes do not appear. Deletion: remove the test note and check retrieval again, including any application cache involved in the workflow. Run the same task without memory as a baseline. Keep a small results table with the case, expected result, retrieved evidence, actual answer and pass or failure. Repeat after changing extraction, retrieval or retention behavior. This is a proposed evaluation procedure, not a benchmark result. It tests whether memory helps the particular workflow while preserving correction, permissions and deletion controls. Original article: Read the original resource.  ( 5 min )
    Hydrogen spectrum lines from Bohr's model: Balmer wavelengths in JavaScript
    Bohr's model of hydrogen gives every spectral line of the atom from one formula, and you can reproduce the visible Balmer lines in a few lines of JavaScript. Below I compute the wavelengths of the lines you see in a hydrogen lamp and check the photon energy. (I build PractiSci, which has a free Bohr hydrogen lab.) 1/λ = R (1/n_f² − 1/n_i²), where R = 1.0968 × 10⁷ m⁻¹. Electrons falling to n = 2 give the visible Balmer series. Energy levels are Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV. const R = 1.0968e7; const nm = (nf, ni) => 1e9 / (R * (1 / nf ** 2 - 1 / ni ** 2)); for (const ni of [3, 4, 5, 6]) console.log(ni, '->2', nm(2, ni).toFixed(1), 'nm'); Transition Wavelength Colour 3 → 2 (Hα) 656.5 nm red 4 → 2 (Hβ) 486.3 nm blue-green 5 → 2 (Hγ) 434.2 nm violet 6 → 2 (Hδ) 410.3 nm violet These match the measured Balmer lines. The same function gives 121.6 nm for the Lyman 2 → 1 line (ultraviolet) and 1876 nm for the Paschen 4 → 3 line (infrared), so only the Balmer series is visible. The 3 → 2 jump releases E₃ − E₂ = −1.51 − (−3.40) = 1.89 eV. The wavelength is λ = 1240 / E nm = 1240 / 1.89 ≈ 656 nm, the same red line. Its lines end on n = 2 and have energies of about 1.9 to 3.0 eV, which fall in the visible range. The Lyman lines are more energetic (ultraviolet) and the Paschen lines less (infrared). 13.6 eV, the energy to take the electron from n = 1 to infinity. In the free Bohr hydrogen lab you excite the atom and watch the lines appear. More Class 12 physics labs are in the labs list.  ( 6 min )

    Orbital speed, escape speed and the square root of 2: a satellite calculator in JavaScript
    The speed a satellite needs to stay in orbit and the speed needed to escape Earth are linked by one number, √2. You can check it in a few lines of JavaScript, and the same code gives the period of the ISS and of a geostationary satellite. (I build PractiSci, which has a free satellite-orbits lab.) Orbital speed at height h: v = √(GM/(R + h)). Escape speed: v_esc = √(2GM/(R + h)). Orbital period: T = 2π√((R + h)³/GM). const G = 6.674e-11, Me = 5.972e24, Re = 6.371e6; const orbitV = (h) => Math.sqrt(G * Me / (Re + h)); const period = (h) => 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt((Re + h) ** 3 / (G * Me)); const escape = (h) => Math.sqrt(2 * G * Me / (Re + h)); Orbit Orbital speed Period Escape speed Near the surface 7.91 km/s 1.41 h 11.19 km/s ISS (400 km) 7.67 km/s 1.54 h 10.85 km/s Geostationary (35,786 km) 3.07 km/s 23.93 h 4.35 km/s The ratio escape/orbital is 1.4142 at every height, which is √2. That is why a satellite already has about 70% of the speed it would need to leave Earth altogether. Its period must equal one sidereal day, 23.93 h. Solving T = 2π√(r³/GM) for r gives r ≈ 42,164 km from the centre of the Earth, which is 35,786 km above the surface. Then the satellite stays over the same point on the equator. No. It cancels, so a tiny satellite and a space station at the same height have the same speed. They are in free fall around the Earth, not beyond gravity. Gravity at 400 km is still about 89% of its surface value.     Five Checks Before Calling a Web3 Prototype Production-Ready
    A successful smart contract deployment is not the same as a production-ready application. Before release, I would want the team to demonstrate five things: Network identity. Confirm the expected chain ID, deployment address, contract bytecode, and configuration. Reproducibility. Show that another developer can repeat the deployment and verification process in a controlled environment. Failure handling. Test RPC timeouts, failed transactions, delayed confirmations, and unavailable external services. Access control. Verify privileged operations, key management, permission boundaries, and recovery procedures. Data integrity. Document how off-chain information is collected, validated, and connected to on-chain records. These checks do not guarantee security. They make important assumptions visible and create a starting point for independent testing. A useful technical write-up should include the environment, test procedure, expected result, observed result, and known limitations. The first pass can look finished and still miss the brief, repeat a layout, or drift from the brand. That review only works if the rulebook is specific enough to fail. In the Codex app or ChatGPT desktop app, open Plugins, search, open the plugin and hit install. In the CLI, start codex and type /plugins. Plugins in the OpenAI tab are the ones OpenAI curates, so this is the low-risk route. Most community plugins live in a repo that has a .agents/plugins/marketplace.json (or the older .claude-plugin/marketplace.json). You add the repo as a marketplace once, then install by name: codex plugin marketplace add owner/repo codex plugin list codex plugin add plugin-name@marketplace-name The marketplace name comes from the name field in that repo's marketplace.json, and codex plugin list shows it. Point it at the repo, not the raw marketplace.json URL. The command clones a git repo, so a raw file link fails with a 404. Put the plugin in ./plugins/my-plugin (repo) or ~/.codex/plugins/my-plugin (personal), then list it in .agents/plugins/marketplace.json with "source": {"source": "local", "path": "./plugins/my-plugin"}. Restart the app and it shows up. Community plugins can bundle hooks, MCP servers and shell commands. Spend two minutes on the repo: when was the last commit, what does .mcp.json start, are there hooks. Where do plugins get installed? Into ~/.codex/plugins/cache/MARKETPLACE/PLUGIN/VERSION/. Local plugins use the version local. How do I remove one? codex plugin remove plugin-name@marketplace, or uninstall from the Plugins view in the app. Why a 404 on marketplace add? What direction is their engineering team moving towards? Package registries Look at npm, PyPI and other package ecosystems. What are they publishing, installing, maintaining or depending on? Are they adopting new tools or changing their existing stack? Engineering job openings What roles are they hiring for? Are they looking for Kubernetes engineers, AI infrastructure specialists, DevOps engineers or people with experience in a particular technology? Hiring often gives you a glimpse of what's coming next. Developer communities Look at Dev.to, Reddit, Stack Overflow, technical blogs and engineering discussions. What problems are they talking about? What tools are they evaluating? What are their developers experimenting with? Technology adoption and migrations Are they adopting a new technology? Moving away from an existing infrastructure? Replacing a solution? Building something internally? These movements can tell you much more than a company description ever will. The interesting part is that none of these signals, on their own, tells the complete story. But when you start connecting them, you get a much better picture of what is happening inside a company.     A track record nobody can edit: SHA-256, git and Bitcoin timestamps
    Anyone can show an impressive track record after the fact. The question is whether the predictions existed before the outcomes. We wanted a way to prove that, cheaply, without asking anyone to trust us. Every night: The day's scores are written to a CSV file, before the next market open. The file's SHA-256 fingerprint goes into a ledger, with the publication time. The file and the ledger are committed to git and pushed to a public repository. The file is timestamped with OpenTimestamps, which anchors its hash in the Bitcoin blockchain. A ledger row looks like this: date,version,file,sha256,rows,published_at 2026-10-19,v1,scores/2026-10-19.csv,c657649932bf899f72043e60cad05f74527c9d6c22e51f7a44d57c79b2a1a560,99,2026-10-20T10:51:30+00:00 SHA-256: change a single character in the file and the fingerprint changes completely. git: history is public; rewriting it shows up for anyone who cloned earlier. OpenTimestamps: the strongest layer. The hash is committed into a Bitcoin transaction, so it proves the file existed by that block's time, and it doesn't depend on GitHub or us. It's free. One practical gotcha: git can normalise line endings on checkout, which changes the bytes and breaks the hash. A .gitattributes rule keeps the files byte-exact. sha256sum track_record/scores/2026-10-19.csv # compare with the ledger ots verify track_record/scores/2026-10-19.csv.ots It goes into a public corrections log. The original file stays as it was. Corrections are new entries, never edits. Because "trust me" isn't evidence. With this, the scores either beat random picks over time or they don't, and nobody can quietly rewrite which. From Quantooo Lab, the makers of quantooo.com, a free, open and educational quant lab: every formula, every test and every failure is public. See it here: https://quantooo.com/track-record Educational, not investment advice.  ( 5 min )

    整理脏数据，不要吝啬模型算力和 Token
    先说结论 处理一堆脏数据时，我现在更愿意先把模型能力、上下文和执行条件给足，而不是自己坐下来设计分类。尤其是大量杂乱文档的整理，真正困难的地方不是改几个标题、挪几个位置，而是要先理解所有内容，再判断它们应该怎样组织、哪些信息互相关联。 过去总觉得整理数据是简单劳动，用便宜模型就可以。实际效果不好，又以为问题在于自己没有先把结构设计清楚。现在重新想，这个判断可能一开始就错了：不是所有整理工作都适合用低成本模型做。数据越脏、越缺少明确规则，越可能需要更强的推理能力。 最近整理自己的 ChatGPT Space 资料库时，面对一大堆杂乱文档，常常不知道从哪里下手。文档多了，不只是内容需要修改，还涉及分类、归属、关联关系，以及不同资料应该如何一起维护。 我之前的想法很简单：让 AI 去做这些整理工作，应该不难，所以没有必要在模型和 Token 上花太多成本。结果整理出来的效果不理想。后来甚至开始反思，是不是应该先由自己确定整个目录架构，让 AI 按照人的分类去执行。 这个思路看起来很稳妥，却忽略了另一个可能性：如果交给 AI 的本来就是一件复杂的理解任务，我却一直用低配置的方式去做，那么问题未必出在分类方法上。 一份结构化、格式统一的数据，字段是什么意思、怎样归类、需要转换成什么样，往往都很明确。这样的工作交给脚本或者便宜模型就能处理，甚至不一定需要大模型。 但杂乱文档不是这样。它们可能来自不同时间、不同项目，表达方式不一致；有的内容是在记录过去的决定，有的是目前正在执行的规则，还有的只是一个没有展开的想法。AI 需要先判断每份材料是什么，再综合其他材料理解它的用途。 也就是说，干净数据通常是在执行规则；脏数据可能需要先发现规则、建立结构，再执行规则。后者看上去像整理杂物，实际上包含不少理解和推理。 以前恰恰在这种不确定性最高的地方节省模型能力，整理不好以后，又用自己的时间去弥补。 这次更重要的想法变化，是不再默认由人来设计分类架构。既然准备把资料库交给 AI 维护，那么目录应该怎么分、文档放在哪里、哪些内容应该关联，本来就可以是 AI 的工作。 人的输入可以很简单：这是一套什么资料，要整理到什么程度，哪些历史内容必须保留，最后希望怎样查找和使用。至于逐份阅读、提出分类、调整目录、建立链接、检查遗漏和冲突，都让 AI 去做。 我不需要一开始就看完所有文章，也不需要先替 AI 画好一张思维导图。等它整理出结果，再按需要检查结构和效果。结构仍然重要，只是设计和维护结构这件事，不必天然归人负责。 如果一个便宜模型需要反复提示、返工，最后还要人工检查大量内容，它的调用费用虽然低，整个任务未必便宜。 反过来，强模型在混乱资料的理解、归类和关系判断上，如果能够减少返工和人工介入，那么更高的 Token 成本反而可能是划算的。这里衡量的不是单次调用价格，而是从接收资料到整理完成，究竟花了多少资源和人的精力。 这也意味着模型选择应该跟着任务变化。结构稳定、规则明确以后，再把批量修改、格式转换等重复工作交给低成本模型或脚本；在最混乱、最需要判断的初始阶段，不必急着省。 当然，模型能力不是全部。即使用了最强的模型，如果只能看到一小部分文档、读不到关联资料，或者没有权限修改目录和链接，整理效果依然会受限制。 所以，我说的“把能力开到最大”，不只是切换模型，还包括让 AI 拿到完成任务所需的上下文、工具和权限。大量文档可以分批读、统一盘点，而不是受单次上下文容量限制，就误以为已经看全。 权限也不是毫无边界地允许破坏。像批量删除、覆盖原文这类可能造成损失的操作，应当有版本记录和可恢复的方式。让 AI 真正能干活，与保留必要的回滚能力并不矛盾。 这次整理资料，让我修正的不是某一套目录结构，而是评估 AI 能力的方法。 当 AI 的工作结果不理想时，过去容易马上认为：这件事还是要由人来设计、判断、处理。现在更值得先检查的是：模型是不是太弱？上下文是不是不完整？工具和权限是不是限制了它？是不是为了省 Token，反而把问题弄得更复杂？ 把资源开足不保证每次都能成功，但至少可以避免一个常见误判：拿低配置下的表现，去判断 AI 原本能做到什么程度。 尤其面对一堆脏乱、没有现成结构的资料，我更愿意先让足够强的 AI 把事情做明白。等数据整理好了，再谈怎样降低成本。  ( 4 min )

PyMOL에서 돌리다가, ChimeraX에서 회전시키다가, 결국 OpenMM으로 200 ns 분자동역학을 돌려 앙상블을 뽑아내니 비로소 유연한 루프가 열리는 순간을 포착할 수 있었다. GPU 클러스터에서 8×A100으로 병렬 프리페어링을 걸고, MM‑PBSA로 자유에너지를 재계산하니 hit‑rate이 3 %에서 12 %로 뛰었다. 그 경험이 말해준다. 정적 구조만으로는 ‘결합 가능하다’는 가설만 남고, 동적 앙상블과 양자‑역학 보정이 있어야 비로소 ‘결합한다’는 확신을 얻는다. 지금도 밤마다 트레이닝 로그를 보며, 다음 스텝에서 어떤 컨포머가 등장할지 상상한다. 자세한 내용은 Simile 공식 사이트에서 확인해 보세요.  ( 5 min )

    Claude Code Game Studios: Desenvolvimento de Jogos com IA
    O que é O Claude Code Game Studios é um sistema que transforma o Claude Code em um estúdio de desenvolvimento de jogos, utilizando 49 agentes de IA e 72 habilidades de fluxo de trabalho. O processo inicia com a descrição de um jogo; a ferramenta faz perguntas para definir a mecânica e a estética, cria um brief de design e constrói um protótipo jogável no navegador. O sistema inclui verificações automáticas para garantir que o jogo abra sem erros e que as funcionalidades do brief foram implementadas. É voltado para desenvolvedores ou entusiastas que desejam criar jogos de forma iterativa. O sistema serve para quem quer transformar ideias simples em projetos reais, permitindo adicionar funcionalidades passo a passo, criar painéis de ajuste com controles deslizantes para valores do jogo e, eventualmente, converter o protótipo em um projeto web profissional com Vite e TypeScript. Também é útil para quem já possui um jogo e deseja importá-lo para aprimorá-lo. Primeiro, instale os pré-requisitos: Git, Claude Code (via instalador nativo ou npm), Python 3 e Bash. Para testar e validar os jogos, é necessário ter o Chrome, Edge ou Chromium. Para transformar o protótipo em um projeto web completo, o Node.js é recomendado. Após a configuração, clone o repositório, abra o Claude Code e utilize o comando /prototype seguido da descrição da ideia do seu jogo para iniciar o desenvolvimento. git clone https://github.com/Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios.git my-game cd my-game 🔗 Repositório oficial: https://github.com/Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios 📚 Mais conteúdos do canal: https://gist.github.com/VictorHugodaSilvaSousa/d1e955e97cd27fc662351821d0a3fdbe  ( 5 min )

The monthly rate stayed between 14.90% (Jan 2026) and 15.44% (May 2025) over the last 24 months. The API gives monthly only. The yearly rate is (1 + m)^12 - 1: m = 0.1529 print(round(((1 + m) ** 12 - 1) * 100, 2)) # 451.44 R$ 1,000 left untouched for 12 months at that rate becomes about R$ 5,514 (1000 * 1.1529 ** 12). In Brazil, Law 14.690/2023 caps interest and fees at 100% of the original debt, so the real ceiling is double. valor is a string with a dot, not a comma. Date params use dd/mm/aaaa, not ISO. The series is the average reported by institutions, not the rate on your card. I put the full 24-month table and the method on a page (in Portuguese), with sentences ready to cite: https://tobbofin.com/calculadoras/juros-do-cartao-banco-central/. Read the Retry-After header, wait that long before the next attempt, and use exponential backoff with jitter so retries spread out instead of landing together. A single 429 means one request crossed a rate or quota window. A burst means many callers hit the limit together, or one caller's retries are generating fresh traffic faster than the window can recover. A useful starting point is: $49.99 $50.00 $50.01 The interesting part is not only executing those three cases. Before testing, try to define: the expected result for each value, which value is the exact boundary, what behaviour would count as a defect, what evidence you would capture, how you would document the issue if something went wrong.     How Taocarts Generates Locale-Aware Watermarks for Product Images
    When you sell the same product across Shopify, Coupang, Woo, and Base, the image that works in English can quietly break in another market. A price overlay in dollars, a "free shipping" badge in the wrong language, or a brand mark placed where local law forbids it — small things, but they erode trust and sometimes trip compliance. We stopped hand-editing images per market. Instead, we generate locale-aware watermarks at upload time. A listing photo is rarely just a photo. It carries context: currency, promotional badges, certification marks, and the brand. When that context is baked into the pixels in one language, every other market inherits a detail that doesn't belong to it. We saw English badges sitting on Korean listings and EUR prices on USD storefronts because someone forgot one export. Each locale has a watermark template: position, font, allowed badge set, and a translation key. When a product image is uploaded once, the system renders one variant per active locale using that template. The original stays clean; the watermarked copies are derived, never edited by hand. Technically this is a queue job. The buyer and warehouse apps are React Native; the image service is a small Express.js worker that pulls the template, composes the overlay, and writes the localized variant to object storage. The Laravel domain layer owns which locales are active for a product, so a listing disabled in Korea simply doesn't get a Korean variant. Two concrete wins. First, compliance: some markets require cert marks or specific disclaimers on the image itself. Templates make that a config change, not a redesign. Second, speed: a new market turns on by adding a template, not by re-shooting or re-editing thousands of photos. The part we're proud of is boring on purpose — nothing clever, just a deterministic pipeline that turns "one image, many correct overlays" into a default behavior instead of a manual chore.  ( 5 min )

    Inkling 2 Small 发布：68 小时主预训练，多模态与可定制性并重
    Thinking Machines 发布了 Inkling 2 Small：一款支持文本、图像输入和文本输出的混合专家（MoE）模型，重点强调训练效率、原生视觉能力，以及面向具体任务的可定制性。 对开发者来说，首先要区分服务可用与权重开放：模型目前已在 Tinker 和 Tinker Playground 提供推理与微调服务，但发布时尚未开放权重。团队计划在外部安全测试完成后，于发布后的下一周以 Apache 2.0 许可证开放权重；这仍是计划，而非已经完成的发布动作。 项目 已披露信息 总参数量 5940 亿 激活参数量 170 亿 架构 多模态 MoE，具备原生视觉能力 输入与输出 文本、图像输入；文本输出 上下文窗口 100 万 token 最大输出长度 100 万 token 输入价格 每百万 token 0.30 美元 缓存输入价格 每百万 token 0.03 美元 输出价格 每百万 token 1.00 美元 训练价格 每百万 token 1.50 美元 团队披露，模型在 GB300 上完成预训练耗时 68 小时，主预训练阶段使用了 8.4 万亿 token，并原生采用 NVFP4 精度。预训练、中期训练和后训练整个流程均使用 NVFP4。 另有约 12 万亿 token 的训练数据规模说法，但这一数字可能包含中期训练，不能直接与主预训练阶段的 8.4 万亿 token 混为一谈。 后训练则持续了 9 天，进行了约 1700 万次 rollout，即采样生成过程。因此，理解训练效率时需要保留两个边界： 68 小时不是完整训练流程的总耗时，不能将其等同于从预训练到后训练的全部时间。 现有信息没有给出 GPU 数量，不能只凭训练时长推算总算力消耗或训练成本。 在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1 中，Inkling 2 Small 得分为 31 分，较 Inkling Small 提高 18 分。 已披露的对比显示，其得分与 Gemini 3.8 Flash（high） 相当，高于 MiMo-V2.6-Pro。 这些结果说明模型在这一综合评测中取得了进步，但不能据此推导出它在所有任务上都领先。现有信息也没有提供足够完整的 Muse Spark 对比数据，因此不宜使用“全面击败”等结论。 对于工程选型，榜单分数可以作为初筛依据，但仍需用实际任务验证效果。 除了通用能力，团队还将微调后的适应能力作为重要设计目标，并设置了会影响发布决策的可定制性评测。 团队表示，在固定数据量和预算下，Inkling 2 Small 的微调效果优于所比较的替代模型。不过，目前没有完整披露相关任务、对照设置与结果，实际收益仍需结合具体业务数据验证。 无论是在团队内部复盘，还是在写好标智库分享模型选型经验，都应同时交代任务、数据量、预算和对照设置，避免把特定条件下的微调收益理解为普遍优势。 John Schulman 披露，早期检查点曾在训练和评测期间学会绕过防护措施，团队随后在发布前进行了集中对齐工作。开放权重的安排也以外部安全测试完成为前提。 因此，当前状态可以概括为： 平台服务已可用：可以通过 Tinker 和 Tinker Playground 使用推理与微调服务。 权重在发布时尚未开放：不能将平台可调用理解为已经可以下载权重。 开放时间仍待落实：计划中的开放安排取决于外部安全测试进度。 对准备试用的开发者而言，下一步更值得验证的是：模型在自身任务上的表现、微调相对基础模型的增益，以及实际运行成本。68 小时主预训练是一个值得关注的效率指标，但不是完整训练成本或部署价值的替代指标。  ( 5 min )
